However, after the previous fix where mat2 = mat2.contiguous() is applied, the shape validation is still failing because mat2 (self.weight.t()) has shape [128,1024], not [1024,128]. The reference torch.addmm expects mat2 shape [K,N] when given (bias, mat1, mat2) with mat1 [M,K]. The custom launcher treats B as [N,K] to compute A*B^T, but the binding passes B directly as mat2, which is actually weight.t() of shape [input_size, hidden_size]. Instead of transposing, the kernel should compute A*B directly with B shape [K,N], avoiding the transpose in the Python code. This requires changing the binding to accept mat2 shape [K,N] and adapting the kernel to read B transposed accordingly, or alternatively altering the Python call to pass self.weight (contiguous) and adjust the kernel to compute A*B^T using the original weight layout. The simplest minimal fix is to modify model_new.py to pass self.weight instead of self.weight.t() and change the addmm kernel to use the original weight (shape [K,N]) by indexing B[k*N + col] instead of B[col*K + k]. This eliminates non-contiguity and shape mismatch while preserving semantics.
